annotations.text:
C · OPS CONSOLE — revised

What changed from the sketch:

1. It doubles. The third artboard is the same screen in the app's existing light tokens, so this is not a dark-only tool. Comms and Legal get a screen they can read.

2. The holding statement is no longer just the first panel. It sits on a lighter ground at 14.5px with an 'external — this one leaves the building' label, because it is the artefact that can do damage.

3. Under it, four chips name the rules it was held to: no cause, no individuals, no assurance of absence, confirmed facts only.

4. Status is now a coloured rail on every timeline row, not only a word — scannable at a glance.

5. The thread pane foots with what did NOT become an event, and says none of it was dropped.

A · DUTY DESK — not taken

The existing app, tightened. Zero learning curve, ships tomorrow.

Why not: nothing about it says the app exercises judgement. It looks like a formatter.

B · EVIDENCE LEDGER — not taken

Provenance as the product: the holding statement as the object that leaves the building, with a margin column listing what was deliberately kept out.

Why not: warm and editorial, slower to scan at 2am. The 'kept out' column is still the best idea in the set — it is a schema change, not a look, so it can be lifted into C.

THE MARK

It is one timeline row, abstracted: the coloured status rail, and the text it stands beside — the single element the Ops Console is built from.

Read the other way it is a blockquote — a statement someone is standing behind, which is what a holding statement is.

The two bars are different lengths on purpose: eighteen messages come in, eight events go out.

No detail exists below what survives at 16px, so the favicon is the logo, not a redraw of it.
